newsitem.title: UK: Safeway sees no impact if min wage 3.50 stg.
newsitem.headline: Safeway sees no impact if min wage 3.50 stg.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc would not see any impact if a proposed minimum wage were set at 3.50 stg per hour, finance director Simon Laffin told Reuters.
"Were it set at 3.50 stg, it wouldn't have an effect, if it were set at 4 stg, it would start to have an impact," he said in a telephone interview.
The Labour government, which swept to power in a landslide victory in a general election on May 1, has said it will introduce a minimum wage but has not yet decided on a level.
Supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc said last week that a minimum wage would have to be over four stg to have an impact, with most of its staff already paid 3.50 stg an hour or above.

Safeway also said that it estimated the cost of adjusting its computer systems for the effect of the change of date in the new millenium would be around five million stg over the next two years. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
